summary: Empty Python FastAPI scaffold for the behaviour-preserving port of the Express 4 'publisher' service (translation pair node-express__python-fastapi), built from the approved system design, mapping plan, feature queue and risk assessment. The publisher/ package holds the nine target module packages in the design's linear build order 0-8 (config, db, notes_cache, memories, templates, tenancy, public_routes, internal_routes, server), each a documentation-only stub with no migrated business behaviour; publisher/module_graph.json records the closed acyclic graph (hyphenated design names mapped to underscore package names). Around it: dependency manifests (pyproject.toml + pinned requirements.txt kept in sync), .env.example covering the full env surface with GHOST_API_KEY as a secret-store placeholder only (ADR-003), a local Postgres 'btw' stack (docker-compose.yml + db/init/01-btw-schema.sql with the four read-only tables), CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) and one stdlib-only smoke check (scripts/smoke.py). All validation commands are argv arrays run from the scaffold root, needing no network, no installed dependencies and no absolute paths.

argv:
import ast, pathlib
files = sorted(pathlib.Path('publisher').rglob('*.py')) + sorted(pathlib.Path('scripts').rglob('*.py'))
for p in files:
    ast.parse(p.read_text(encoding='utf-8'), filename=str(p))
print('syntax OK:', len(files), 'python files')
validation.purpose: Syntax-check every scaffold Python file via ast.parse; unlike compileall this writes no bytecode caches, so rerunning validation leaves the tree clean.
Prove the target module graph manifest is valid JSON.

Smoke check (stdlib-only, clean checkout): all nine module packages import; the module graph is closed and acyclic with every depends_on at a strictly smaller build_order and a matching package directory; .env.example declares every required env var with GHOST_API_KEY as a secret-store placeholder; no file contains the leaked GHOST_API_KEY literal (ADR-003); requirements.txt pins every dependency with == and its set equals pyproject.toml dependencies; every manifest-listed file exists and every validation step is a non-empty argv array of strings; docker-compose.yml defines the local Postgres btw stack.

notes: All validation commands are argv arrays of strings relative to the scaffold root — no shell strings, no quoting, no globbing, no absolute paths — and need no network access or third-party packages, so they run from a clean checkout. The syntax step uses ast.parse instead of compileall so rerunning validation writes no __pycache__ bytecode into the tree.

Dependency installation (python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt) is exercised in CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml), not in the local validation commands, keeping the local checks fast and self-contained; the smoke check itself passes with no dependencies installed because the scaffold stubs are docstring-only.

The scaffold contains no migrated business behaviour: every publisher/<module>/__init__.py is a documentation-only stub recording responsibilities, source modules, depends_on and the explicit dead-code drops (utils/utils.js, routes/sitemap.js genSitemap() — ADR-010).

GHOST_API_KEY is never written into this repository (ADR-003): .env.example carries a <load-from-secret-store> placeholder and scripts/smoke.py assembles the leaked source literal from two fragments and scans every scaffold file for it, so the checker file itself never contains the secret.

Hyphenated design module names map to Python packages with underscores (notes-cache -> notes_cache, public-routes -> public_routes, internal-routes -> internal_routes); the mapping is machine-readable in publisher/module_graph.json.

db/init/01-btw-schema.sql creates only the read-only tables the service touches (btw.users, btw.custom_domains, btw.notes, btw.memories) with column definitions taken from the recorded btw pg_dump, for the local docker-compose stack on localhost:55432.

Build-order rule for future work: a module may only import modules with a strictly smaller build_order; scripts/smoke.py enforces this invariant on publisher/module_graph.json so the graph cannot silently become cyclic or forward-referencing.
